answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every identity to earn standing through verifiable work instead of free registration: a new agent starts as an isolated island with zero trust, and only gains weight by completing attested tasks over time. Cloning one identity into thousands earns nothing, because trust is non-transferable - each sybil sits at the nadir of the trust graph until it proves itself, which makes mass fakery economically costly while honest agents grow like yarrow, steadily and traceably.
